[[File:火男火女神社1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Torii]]
'''Hinohonome Shrine''' (火男火売神社, also '''Hinohonome Shrine''' (火男火賣神社)) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Ōita Prefecture|en|Ōita Prefecture|qid=Q133924|lt=Oita Prefecture|1=Ōita Prefecture}} {{ill|Beppu|en|Beppu|qid=Q273880|lt=Beppu City|1=Beppu}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, and its former shrine Rank was that of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}, as categorized under the modern shrine Ranking system (see {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}).
It consists of three shrines:
- Upper Shrine (Oku-no-miya) located at the summit of {{ill|Mount Tsurumi|en|Mount Tsurumi|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama|1=Mount Tsurumi}},
- Middle Shrine (Higashiyama) on the mid-slope (also known as '''Mitake Gongen''' <おたけごんげん>),
- Lower Shrine (Sato-no-miya) at the foot (also known as '''Tsurumi Gongen''').
== Worshipped Deities (Saijin) ==
{{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}}
* Upper Shrine: {{ill|Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto|ja|火之加具土命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto|qq=}} (ほのかぐつちのみこと), and Hiyaki Hayame no Mikoto (ひやきはやめのみこと)
* Middle Shrine: Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto, and Hiyaki Hayame no Mikoto
* Lower Shrine: {{ill|Izanagi|en|Izanagi|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi|1=Izanagi}}, {{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami|1=Izanami}}, Hinokagutsuchi no Kami (火之加具土神), and {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|qid=Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}
== History ==
=== Founding ===
According to shrine tradition, the enshrinement was established in {{ill|771|ja|771|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/771|qq=}} (Hōki 2, {{ill|Hōki|en|Hōki|qid=Q18520676|lt=宝亀|1=Hōki}} 2).
The deities that give the shrine its name, {{ill|Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto|ja|火之加具土命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokagutsuchi no Mikoto|qq=}} and Hiyaki Hayame no Mikoto (火焼速女命), are thought to be the deification of the two peaks of {{ill|Sacred mountains|en|Sacred mountains|qid=Q1595289|lt=Sacred Mountain|1=Sacred mountains}} ({{ill|Mount Tsurumi|en|Mount Tsurumi|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama|1=Mount Tsurumi}}) into male and female deities. It was widely known from ancient times that there were {{ill|Onsen|en|Onsen|qid=Q655311|lt=Onsen|1=Onsen}} at the foot of {{ill|Mount Tsurumi|en|Mount Tsurumi|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama|1=Mount Tsurumi}} in {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|qid=Q864148|lt=Bungo Province|1=Bungo Province}}'s {{ill|Hayami District, Ōita|en|Hayami District, Ōita|qid=Q1043858|lt=Hayami District|1=Hayami District, Ōita}}, but due to the active eruptions of Tsurumi-yama, the area had become barren land and marshes, and was left undeveloped. Both the {{ill|Bungo Fudoki|ja|豊後国風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bungo Fudoki|qq=}} and the {{ill|Man'yōshū|en|Man'yōshū|qid=Q834321|lt=Man'yōshū|1=Man'yōshū}} mention features such as the "Akayu Spring" (赤湯の泉) corresponding to what is now the {{ill|Blood Pond Hell|ja|血の池地獄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Blood Pond Hell|qq=}} at {{ill|Shibaishi Onsen|ja|柴石温泉|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shibaishi Onsen|qq=}}, and the "Kuberi-yu no I" (玖倍理湯の井) corresponding to the hellish area of {{ill|Tetsunawa Onsen|ja|鉄輪温泉|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsunawa Onsen|qq=}}. Furthermore, an excerpt from the {{ill|Iyo Fudoki|ja|伊予国風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Fudoki|qq=}} recounts a {{ill|Myth|en|Myth|qid=Q12827256|lt=myth|1=Myth}} in which {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} directed a conduit from the "Hayami no Yu" ({{ill|Hayami no Yu|ja|速見の湯|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayami no Yu|qq=}}) spring, which emerges at the foot of Tsurumi-yama—the shrine's shintai—to {{ill|Dōgo Onsen|en|Dōgo Onsen|qid=Q1037748|lt=Dōgo Onsen|1=Dōgo Onsen}}, thereby healing the illness of {{ill|Sukunahikona no Mikoto|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunahikona no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}.
== Overview ==
According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}<ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 2月26日"/> <ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 4月3日">According to the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku, entry of April 3, 867 (Jōgan 9).</ref>, when {{ill|867|ja|867|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/867|qq=}} (Jōgan 9) on {{ill|January 20|en|January 20|qid=Q2267|lt=January 20|1=January 20}}, an eruption occurred at {{ill|Mount Tsurumi|en|Mount Tsurumi|qid=Q6924219|lt=Tsurumi-yama|1=Mount Tsurumi}}, and at the command of the Court to the provincial governor of {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|qid=Q864148|lt=Bungo Province|1=Bungo Province}}, the {{ill|Large Prajñāpāramitā Sūtras|en|Large Prajñāpāramitā Sūtras|qid=Q15905785|lt=Great Prajna Sutra|1=Large Prajñāpāramitā Sūtras}} was recited before the shrine.
In {{ill|927|ja|927|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927|qq=}} (Enchō 5) the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} was established, wherein the shrine is recorded as "Hinohonome Shrine Two-seat" in {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|qid=Q864148|lt=Bungo Province|1=Bungo Province}}'s {{ill|Hayami District, Ōita|en|Hayami District, Ōita|qid=Q1043858|lt=Hayami District|1=Hayami District, Ōita}}, and it is listed among the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} alongside {{ill|Unagi Hime Shrine|ja|宇奈岐日女神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Unagi Hime Shrine|qq=}} in Hayami District.
In {{ill|1276|ja|1276|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1276|qq=}} (Kenji 2), the itinerant monk {{ill|Ippen|en|Ippen|qid=Q1056232|lt=Ippen|1=Ippen}}, who was traveling across Kyushu, is said to have stopped in Beppu and, guided by Tsurumi Gongen, pacified the "Kuberi-yu no I", thereby opening the stone bath (currently known as {{ill|Tetsunawa Mushiyu|ja|鉄輪むし湯|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsunawa Mushiyu|qq=}}) at {{ill|Tetsunawa Onsen|ja|鉄輪温泉|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tetsunawa Onsen|qq=}}. Consequently, the shrine has been venerated as the guardian deity of the {{ill|Beppu Hachiyu|ja|別府八湯|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppu Hachiyu|qq=}}.
During the Tenshō era, the shrine buildings were burned by {{ill|Otomo Sōrin|ja|大友宗麟|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomo Sōrin|qq=}}, and many ancient documents were lost, but the Lower Shrine was rebuilt in {{ill|1664|ja|1664|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1664|qq=}} (Kanbun 4) by Kurushima Dōsei. The area around the Lower Shrine, Tsurumi Village, became an exclave of the Mori Domain, and the {{ill|Myōban Onsen|ja|明礬温泉|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōban Onsen|qq=}} produced {{ill|Myōban|ja|明礬|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōban|qq=}} (also known as {{ill|Onsen Flakes|ja|湯の花|1=Yunohana|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen Flakes|13=User:Immanuelle/Yunohana|qq=}}), which served as an important source of revenue for the domain.
=== Shrine Ranks ===
* In Kakyō 2 ({{ill|849|ja|849|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/849|qq=}}) on June 1, the deity Hinokahime was accorded the Junior Fifth Rank, Lower. <ref group="原">From the Zoku Nihon Kōki, Kakyō 2, June 1.</ref>
* In Jōgan 9 ({{ill|867|ja|867|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/867|qq=}}) on February 26, records indicate that the deities {{ill|Hinokami|ja|火男神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami|qq=}} and Honomai were accorded the Junior Fifth Rank, Upper and Lower respectively. <ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 2月26日">From the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku, entry of February 26, 867.</ref>
* On August 16, 867 (Jōgan 9), both the deity {{ill|Hinokami|ja|火男神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinokami|qq=}} and the deity {{ill|Honomai|ja|火咩神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honomai|qq=}}, both of Junior Fifth Rank, Upper, were jointly conferred the Senior Fifth Rank, Lower. <ref group="原" name="貞観9th year 8月16日">From the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku, entry of August 16, 867.</ref>
== Cultural Properties ==
=== Oita Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Properties ===
* The pagoda of the deity of the Sacred Peak at the Middle Shrine – located at the Middle Shrine. Designated on March 28, Showa 50.<ref name="文化財">[http://www.city.beppu.oita.jp/education/shogaigakusyuuka/bunkazai.htm Beppu City's Designated Cultural Properties] (Beppu City Lifelong Learning Division website).</ref>
=== Oita Prefecture Designated Natural Monuments ===
* The Ichiigashi forest of the Tsurumi Gongen Shrine – located at the Lower Shrine. Designated on March 28, Showa 50.<ref name="文化財"/>
* The natural forest of the deity of the Sacred Peak at the Middle Shrine – located at the Middle Shrine. Designated on March 28, Showa 50.<ref name="文化財"/>
Furthermore, the forest of Hinohonome Shrine (Tsurumi, Beppu City) was designated as a specially protected tree area in {{ill|1974|ja|1974|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1974|qq=}} (Showa 49) on {{ill|March 15|en|March 15|qid=Q2403|lt=March 15|1=March 15}}.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.pref.oita.jp/uploaded/attachment/100227.pdf|title=Oita Prefecture Environmental White Paper|page=44|publisher=Oita Prefecture|accessdate=2024-09-02}}</ref>
